summary: This informational document sets policy for including Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) in the definitive versions of RFCs and related publication formats. It keeps the policy requirements from RFC 7996 but drops requirements about a specific SVG profile or implementation code, and it obsoletes RFC 7996.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9896 sets policy for SVG drawings included in RFCs and related publication formats. It leaves decisions about SVG tools and implementation to the RFC Production Center while requiring that diagrams support, rather than replace, the RFC text.

subtitle: Policy for SVG drawings in RFCs, with tooling decisions assigned to the RFC Production Center.

tldr.problem: RFC 7996 combined policy about SVG drawings with requirements for a particular SVG profile and implementation code.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9896 keeps policy requirements, removes profile and implementation-code requirements, and assigns tooling decisions to the RFC Production Center.
tldr.outcome: This Informational RFC obsoletes RFC 7996. SVG must not contain animation, executable script, or pointers to external resources, and cannot be the only representation of a concept.

sections.title: Policy and Tooling Responsibility
sections.content:
This document sets policy for including Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) in definitive RFC versions and relevant publication formats. It retains policy requirements from RFC 7996 but removes requirements tied to a specific SVG profile or implementation code.

The RFC Production Center (RPC) makes decisions about SVG tooling and implementation. It may use RFC 7996 as a starting point but is not bound by it.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC sets rules for SVG drawings in RFC publications. The RPC chooses the tools and implementation details that follow those rules.

sections.title: Requirements for SVG Drawings
sections.content:
SVG drawings may help explain a concept, but they should not be its only representation. The RFC text should fully represent protocols, formats, and architectures, and drawings must be consistent with that text.

SVG drawings MUST NOT contain animation, interactive features, pointers to external resources, or executable script. They should be accessible to a wide audience. Authors may include multiple image versions in RFCXML, and publication formats should present versions suited to each format.
sections.plainLanguage: A diagram can help explain a concept, but the RFC text must also explain it. SVG drawings must not animate, run scripts, or fetch external resources.

sections.title: RPC Guidance and Review
sections.content:
The RPC may set technical and editorial constraints on SVG to ensure policy compliance and consistency across the RFC Series. It must document acceptable SVG usage and widely communicate changes to tooling and implementation decisions.

The RPC is expected to solicit community input and explain its reasoning publicly. Its implementation should support widely used drawing tools where possible and focus on describing what is disallowed. Practices should be reviewed periodically.
sections.plainLanguage: The RPC must document SVG rules and communicate changes to RFC authors. It should seek community input, explain decisions, and review its practices.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The RFC states that it has no security considerations and no IANA actions. Its policy requirements still prohibit executable script and external resource pointers in drawings.
sections.plainLanguage: The document states that it raises no security considerations and requires no IANA actions. Its policy forbids SVG scripts and external resource pointers.
